# pycubrid

> Pure-Python DB-API 2.0 (PEP 249) driver for the CUBRID database, with an asyncio API (`pycubrid.aio`). No C extensions and no runtime dependencies except `tzdata` on Windows (for time zone names); Python 3.10+, PEP 561 typed.

pycubrid implements the CUBRID CAS (broker) wire protocol in Python. It provides synchronous `pycubrid.connect()` and asynchronous `pycubrid.aio.connect()` connections, is tested against CUBRID 10.2, 11.0, 11.2 and 11.4, and is the recommended driver for sqlalchemy-cubrid.

Key facts:
- PEP 249 globals: `apilevel = "2.0"`, `threadsafety = 1` (threads may share the module, not connections), `paramstyle = "qmark"`
- Connect: `pycubrid.connect(host="localhost", port=33000, database="testdb", user="dba", password="")`; async: `await pycubrid.aio.connect(...)` with the same arguments
- Charset: `connect(..., charset="utf-8")` (sync and async) sets the codec for SQL text, credentials, character values, column names and error text; use the database charset, e.g. `charset="euckr"`. CUBRID names `utf8`/`euckr`/`iso88591` are accepted, codecs that are not ASCII-transparent are rejected, JSON is always UTF-8, and the broker does no conversion, so a mismatch raises `DataError`
- Autocommit is off by default; toggle with `conn.autocommit = True` (async: `await conn.set_autocommit(True)`) or `connect(..., autocommit=True)`
- Parameter binding is driver-side: `cursor.execute(sql, params)` renders `?` placeholders into escaped SQL literals on the client and sends one complete SQL string per execute. Ordinary sync and async cursors send no typed value payload, keep no driver-side statement-handle cache and have no `cursor.prepare()`; server-side plan caching is outside the driver contract
- Binding limits: parameters must be a sequence (mappings are rejected); `None`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `Decimal`, `str`, `bytes`/`bytearray`, `date`, `time` and `datetime` are supported, anything else raises `ProgrammingError`; a list or tuple is not expanded for `IN (...)`; identifiers (including `callproc` names) are never bound
- The only prepared API is the opt-in, sync-only `pycubrid.compat.native` cursor (`prepare()` / `bind_param()` for INT32, string and NULL values; strings use the connection charset); it is a bounded compatibility subset, not a general DB-API cursor
- `executemany()` sends INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE rows as one batch request (other statements fall back to a per-row loop); `executemany_batch(sql_list)` sends a list of SQL strings in one request
- `callproc()` runs `CALL name(?, ...)` and returns the input parameters unchanged; the function's return value is the single row of the result (`fetchone()`), decoded like a column value (`CALL`/`EVALUATE` cells carry their own type, #542); `nextset()` raises `NotSupportedError`
- Exceptions: `Warning`, `Error`, `InterfaceError`, `DatabaseError`, `DataError`, `OperationalError`, `IntegrityError`, `InternalError`, `ProgrammingError`, `NotSupportedError`, with `errno` / `sqlstate` on database errors
- Type objects `STRING`, `BINARY`, `NUMBER`, `DATETIME`, `ROWID` and the PEP 249 constructors (`Date`, `Time`, `Timestamp`, `Binary`, `*FromTicks`)
- Also: LOBs via `conn.create_lob()`, schema introspection via `get_schema_info()`, `get_last_insert_id()`, `ping()`, `get_server_version()`, opt-in TLS (`ssl=True` or an `ssl.SSLContext`), opt-in collection decoding (`decode_collections=True`) and JSON decoding (`json_deserializer=`), context managers and cursor iteration (sync and async)
- Install: `pip install pycubrid`

## Docs

- [Quick Start](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/quickstart/): Install, connect, CRUD and explicit transactions
- [Connection Guide](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/CONNECTION/): `connect()` parameters, TLS, context managers, autocommit, broker handshake, pooling
- [API Reference](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/API_REFERENCE/): `connect()`, `pycubrid.aio`, Connection, Cursor, Lob, exceptions, type objects, the explicit native compatibility subset
- [Parameter Binding](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/PARAMETER_BINDING/): Authoritative driver-side binding contract, type-to-literal mapping, escaping and limits
- [Type Mapping](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/TYPES/): CUBRID types to Python, type objects and constructors, LOB and collection types
- [Examples](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/EXAMPLES/): TLS, CRUD, transactions, parameterized queries, batches, LOBs, schema introspection, stored procedures

## Reference

- [Protocol](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/PROTOCOL/): CAS wire protocol, packets and function codes
- [Architecture](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/ARCHITECTURE/): Module structure, CAS reconnection, public API boundary
- [Support Matrix](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/SUPPORT_MATRIX/): Python and CUBRID version compatibility and per-feature status
- [Official Driver API Inventory](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/pycubrid/UPSTREAM_COMPATIBILITY/): Differences from the official CUBRIDdb driver and the selected compatibility contract
- [Source — cursor.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/pycubrid/blob/main/pycubrid/cursor.py): Cursor — execute, executemany, executemany_batch, fetch, callproc, iterator
- [Source — connection.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/pycubrid/blob/main/pycubrid/connection.py): Connection — connect, commit, rollback, cursor, autocommit, LOB, schema info
- [Source — aio](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/pycubrid/tree/main/pycubrid/aio): AsyncConnection and AsyncCursor

## Examples

- [README Quick Start](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/pycubrid/blob/main/README.md#quick-start): Connection, context managers, parameter binding, async
- [Cookbook — pycubrid fundamentals](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/pycubrid): Numbered pycubrid examples from connect to cascade delete
- [Cookbook — Parameterized queries](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/parameterized-queries): `?` placeholders with driver-side binding
- [Cookbook — Async](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/async): `pycubrid.aio` and the SQLAlchemy async engine
- [Cookbook — LOB handling](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/lob-handling): BLOB/CLOB with `conn.create_lob()`

## Ecosystem

- [sqlalchemy-cubrid](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid): SQLAlchemy 2.0/2.1 dialect for CUBRID (`cubrid+pycubrid://`, `cubrid+aiopycubrid://`)
- [cubrid-cookbook-python](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python): Runnable Python examples for CUBRID
- [CUBRID](https://www.cubrid.org/): The CUBRID database
